chapter: Faking parts and the Tuxedo bands
title: No written orchestrations; parts were faked
summary: Ridgley explains the band got the melody and the rest faked their parts. There were no orchestrations for tunes like The Saints, a church hymn.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: the time, which was made up. And we would get an orchestra, you know, orchestration, and if we could get the melody of it, the lead like that, you see, the rest of us would fake our way through, make our parts. Make your parts. Make our parts like that.

If you wanted, if you had the money and wanted to buy the orchestrated parts, they wouldn't have been available anyway, would they? I mean... We couldn't handle them. We couldn't play them all. Were they even written? I mean, say, the orchestration to the saints, was that

written anywhere, the trombone part? No. No. That's the old Baptist hymn when the saints go marching in. Now that was for church, you know, the hymn. And they're taking it, and just like you see them playing today, there wasn't no dancing or nothing like that kind.
So there wasn't any Dixieland orchestrated music that you could buy if you had the money?
